in_arabic.name: عثمان
in_arabic.meaning: العثمان هو من أسماء الصحابة والتابعين
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم عثمان مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ع-ث-م' الذي يعني الثروة والغنى، وكان اسمًا شائعًا بين الصحابة والتابعين، ويعتبر من الأسماء المحببة في الإسلام نظرًا لارتباطها بالخليفة عثمان بن عفان، أحد أصحاب النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

in_urdu.name: عثمان
in_urdu.meaning: عثمان نام اچھا اور مبارک ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: عثمان نام کی اصل عربی ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے دولت مند اور ثروتマンド۔ یہ نام اسلامی تاریخ میں بہت اہمیت رکھتا ہے کیونکہ عثمان بن عفان رسول اللہ صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم کے مشہور صحابیوں میں سے ایک تھے اور انھوں نے خلافت راشدہ میں اہم کردار ادا کیا تھا۔

in_pashto.name: عثمان
in_pashto.meaning: عثمان نوم دى پخوا د خليفې نوم
in_pashto.long_meaning: عثمان نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې ده بډایه او شتمن. دا نوم د اسلامي تاريخ په منځ کې ډیر اهمیت لري ځکه چې عثمان بن عفان د پيغمبر محمد صلی الله عليه وسلم يو له مشهور صحابیو څخه و او د خلافت په تاريخ کې يې مهم رول لوبولی دی.

in_english.meaning: Derived from Arabic root, meaning wealthy, rich or prosperous

It holds significant historical and spiritual importance in Islam as it was the name of Uthman ibn Affan, one of the most prominent companions of Prophet Muhammad and the third Caliph of Islam. The name symbolizes blessings, prosperity, and a strong connection to Islamic heritage.

data.cultural_impact: The name Uthmaanun holds a significant place in Islamic history as it is the name of one of the Rashidun Caliphs, Uthman ibn Affan (ra). He is considered the third leading caliph in the early Islamic period, succeeding Abu Bakr As-Siddiq and Umar ibn Al-Khattab. Uthman's reign is often seen as a period of peace and consolidation, during which the Quran was compiled into its present form. The name "Uthman" has been passed down through generations and is still a common name among Muslims today, emphasizing the importance of leadership, guidance, and assistance in Islamic society.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, the name Uthmaanun represents the idea of being a person of guidance and support. The Arabic term "uthman" (وثنان) is constructed from the letters waw, tha', and nun. These letters have meanings associated with progress, guidance, and the pursuit of knowledge. As such, the name can be interpreted as one who is frequently sought for guidance or assistance, paralleling the prophetic hadith, "Consult people of knowledge." By embracing this name, one is reminded to strive towards becoming a guide and source of support for their family, community, and even the world at large.

historical_references.reference: Uthman ibn Affan was the third caliph (ruling leader) of the early Islamic ummah (community). He ruled from 656 CE to 656 CE. Uthman is considered one of the Rashidun Caliphs and is also known as Uthman ibn Affan ibn Abi Al-Aas. He was a close companion of Prophet Muhammad and was instrumental in the preservation of the Quran. During his reign, the second caliph, Umar ibn Al-Khattab, was assassinated, and Uthman was elected by the community to be the new caliph. He ruled with justice and fairness and continued the successful political and military expansion of the Islamic state.
historical_references.context: Immediately after the death of Prophet Muhammad, Uthman was elected as the new caliph by the community. He is considered one of the Rashidun Caliphs, known for his just and fair rulership.

historical_references.reference: Uthman ibn Affan was a prominent companion of Prophet Muhammad and played a significant role in the early development of the Islamic community. He was a wealthy merchant from Mecca and was a cousin of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth caliph, and the husband of Aisha bint Abu Bakr, another prominent companion of the Prophet. Uthman played a crucial role in the preservation of the Quran, arranging for its compilation and standardization in written form. During his caliphate, he oversaw the construction of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, a significant architectural and religious achievement for the early Islamic community. He was assassinated in 656 CE during a period of political instability and unrest in the Islamic state.
historical_references.context: Uthman was a prominent companion of Prophet Muhammad and played a crucial role in the preservation and standardization of the Quran. He also oversaw the construction of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem during his caliphate.

modern_usage.modern_context: Uthmanun, also known as Uthman ibn Affan, is a significant figure in Islamic history and studies. His life and contributions continue to be a subject of interest and research in various academic circles. Uthman was the third caliph of Islam, succeeding Abu Bakr and Umar ibn al-Khattab. He oversaw the consolidation of the Islamic state and the compilation of the Quran into its present form. Uthman is revered as a hero for his unwavering commitment to the faith and his efforts to maintain unity among Muslims. His legacy is explored in depth on various academic platforms such as Academia.edu, ResearchGate, and Arabic Wikipedia, where scholars share their findings, insights, and perspectives on Uthman's life, character, and significance in Islamic history.
